title: NETWORK: One Minute Wonder at RUB University Hospitals
summary:
Background
Continuous education and training are important for high-quality patient care. One Minute Wonder (OMW) offer learning opportunities with condensed content where employees regularly have short waiting times in daily practice (e.g. at the elevator, microwave oven, etc.). This form of learning is also used in the university hospitals of the Ruhr University Bochum, among others. To date, there are only a few internationally and nationally published evaluation results following the implementation of OMW within various areas of hospitals.
Aim
The primary objective of this study is to find out to what extent nursing staff use OMW as an educational method in practice and how they evaluate it. Secondary objectives include the subjective educational gain, administrative framework conditions and factors that inhibit and promote the implementation of OMW.
Method
Multi-center study in six university hospitals of the Ruhr University Bochum. A quantitative survey is to be conducted using standardized questionnaires with approx. 3700 nurses in wards with beds and functional areas. In order to identify factors that inhibit and promote the implementation of OMW, two focus group interviews will be conducted with six people as nursing staff at each university hospital respectively and analyzed by using Kuckartz content analysis.
Expected results
The results of this study should generate insights into the application and optimization of OMW in the Ruhr University Bochum hospitals.
conditions: The subject of this study is not a disease‑related condition, but an organizational and health care–related problem within the nursing context. The study investigates the implementation and use of the knowledge‑transfer format One Minute Wonder (OMW) in clinical nursing practice at the university hospitals of Ruhr University Bochum (RUB).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Affiliation with a nursing profession at one of the university hospitals of Ruhr University Bochum, including registered nurses, nursing assistants, nursing trainees, and nursing students
Employment or placement in a ward with inpatient beds or in a functional department of the participating hospitals
Willingness to participate voluntarily in the written questionnaire and/or focus group interviews
Exclusion criteria:
Observers, interns, temporary staff working fewer than 3 days on the ward, international nursing students completing their training, and all records of individuals who answered fewer than 50% of the questions.
